stories.headline: Intel and AMD lock Chinese data centers into long-term CPU contracts as prices jump 40%

key_facts.fact: Intel and AMD are signing longer-term purchase commitments with Chinese server customers for data-center processors as prices surge, according to two people familiar with the talks (reported July 23).
key_facts.excerpt: BEIJING, July 23 (Reuters) – U.S. chipmaking giants Intel and Advanced Micro Devices are signing longer-term purchase commitments with Chinese server customers for data-centre processors as prices surge, two people familiar with the talks said.

key_facts.fact: The agreements lock in purchase volumes but not prices; most cover about a year of supply, though Intel and AMD have discussed commitments of two years or longer with some customers.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreements under discussion typically lock in purchase volumes but not prices, the people said. Most cover about a year of supply, although Intel and AMD have discussed commitments of two years or longer from some customers, one of the people said.

key_facts.fact: Server CPU prices in China are still climbing, with month-on-month increases topping 10% for some products, and some CPU products up more than 40% since the start of the year.
key_facts.excerpt: Server CPU prices are still climbing in China, with month-on-month increases topping 10% for some products, one of the sources said. Prices of some CPU products have risen more than 40% in China since the start of the year, the source added.

key_facts.fact: The shift marks a change for server CPUs, which had been easier to obtain than AI accelerators or memory chips; Intel earlier this year warned Chinese customers of lead times as long as six months for some products.
key_facts.excerpt: The talks mark a shift for server CPUs, which have been easier to obtain than AI accelerators or memory chips. ... Reuters reported earlier this year that Intel and AMD had notified Chinese customers of lengthy waits for server CPUs, with Intel lead times reaching as long as six months for some products.

key_facts.fact: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan told analysts in April that demand 'continues to run ahead of supply,' especially for Xeon server CPUs, and cited a multi-year deal with Google among long-term contracts signed in the first quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: CEO Lip-Bu Tan told analysts in April that demand "continues to run ahead of supply," especially for Xeon server CPUs. He also cited a multi-year deal with Google as one of several long-term contracts Intel signed in the first quarter.

key_facts.fact: Chinese buyers can still purchase US server CPUs freely even as they face separate US restrictions on the most advanced AI GPUs; AMD has raised its server CPU market forecast to more than $120 billion by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: already raised its server CPU market forecast to more than $120 billion by 2030 ... The buildout has intensified competition for Intel and AMD processors, even as Chinese buyers face separate U.S. restrictions on access to the most advanced AI GPUs.

stories.headline: Travis Kalanick's robotics company Atoms raises $1.7B led by a16z, with Uber joining

key_facts.fact: Atoms, Travis Kalanick's robotics and industrial-AI company, announced a $1.7 billion funding round led by Andreessen Horowitz on July 22; Ben Horowitz joins the board.
key_facts.excerpt: Travis Kalanick's robotics company, Atoms, has raised $1.7 billion in a funding round led by Andreessen Horowitz. Ben Horowitz will join the company's board following the investment.

key_facts.fact: Uber joined the round, reconnecting Kalanick with the company he founded and that pushed him out as CEO in 2017.
key_facts.excerpt: Perhaps most notably, Uber also joined the funding round, re-connecting Kalanick with the company he founded — and the same company that pushed him out as CEO in 2017.

key_facts.fact: Kalanick said the round comes with a merger of his various businesses into a single Atoms equity structure, framing it as finishing the 'bits-to-atoms' arc started at Uber and continued at CloudKitchens.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, ATOMS is announcing a $1.7B equity investment with lead investor A16Z and Ben Horowitz joining the board. As part of this investment we have merged our various businesses into one Atoms equity structure.

key_facts.fact: Atoms is organized into three units — Atoms Food, Atoms Mining and Atoms Transport — and Horowitz says Kalanick has been building the company for eight years, largely in stealth.
key_facts.excerpt: We're backing Travis Kalanick's "new" company, Atoms, and I'm joining the board. ... Travis has actually been working on Atoms for 8 years. ... He has three of them so far: Atoms Food, Atoms Mining, and Atoms Transport.

key_facts.fact: Atoms is a rebranded holding company built atop CloudKitchens; in March Kalanick disclosed the acquisition of Pronto, the heavy-industry automation company run by former Uber colleague Anthony Levandowski. Kalanick has said he wants to build a 'wheelbase for robots.'
key_facts.excerpt: Atoms is essentially a rebranded holding company created atop the project Kalanick has been working on since he resigned from Uber, a ghost kitchen play called Cloud Kitchens. When he revealed the new name in March, Kalanick announced he had acquired Pronto, the heavy industry automation company run by his former Uber colleague Anthony Levandowski. ... Kalanick has said he wants to build a "wheelbase for robots" with Atoms.

key_facts.fact: The financing includes both equity and debt, and targets automation in mining, construction, heavy transport and food production.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal includes both equity and debt financing, with Uber among the companies backing Kalanick's latest venture. ... The funding will support Atoms' efforts to develop physical automation systems for large industrial sectors, including mining, construction, heavy transport and food production.

stories.headline: Google starts selling TPU systems as hardware and lifts 2026 capex to as much as $205B

key_facts.fact: Alphabet's Q2 filing states that Google Cloud 'generates product revenues primarily from the sale of TPU systems,' alongside services revenue from consumption fees and subscriptions.
key_facts.excerpt: Google Cloud generates services revenues primarily from consumption-based fees and subscriptions received for Google Cloud Platform services, Google Workspace communication and collaboration tools, and other enterprise services. Google Cloud generates product revenues primarily from the sale of TPU systems.

key_facts.fact: On the earnings call, Alphabet said it began recognizing revenue from TPU system sales delivered to customer data centers for the first time in Q2, and that Cloud growth accelerated even excluding those sales.
key_facts.excerpt: We also began to recognize revenues from TPU system sales, which we delivered to customer data centers for the first time in Q2. Cloud revenue growth accelerated meaningfully even after excluding the impact of TPU system sales.

key_facts.fact: Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year over year to $24.8 billion in Q2, with operating income of $8.8 billion and a backlog of $514 billion, up more than $50 billion sequentially.
key_facts.excerpt: Cloud revenue grew 82%, powered by strong demand for AI infrastructure and AI solutions. ... Cloud operating income was $8.8 billion, more than tripling year-over-year, and operating margin increased from 20.7% ... to 35.6%. Google Cloud's backlog increased by more than $50 billion sequentially, reaching $514 billion in the second quarter.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet raised full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195-$205 billion from $180-$190 billion, citing accelerated delivery of capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: Moving to investments, we are updating our full year 2026 capex guidance range to $195 billion to $205 billion, up from our previous estimate of $180 billion to $190 billion. The increase in the range is primarily due to an acceleration in the delivery of capacity to meet growing demand.

key_facts.fact: Q2 purchases of property and equipment totaled $44.9 billion and non-GAAP free cash flow was negative $5.86 billion, against $39.1 billion of operating cash flow.
key_facts.excerpt: Non-GAAP free cash flow for Q2 2026 was $(5,855) million. Net cash provided by operating activities was $39,069 million, while purchases of property and equipment totaled $44,924 million, reflecting substantial capital investment, including efforts to scale AI infrastructure and global compute capacity.

key_facts.fact: Management said roughly 60% of the capex goes to servers and 40% to data centers and networking equipment, and that most TPU system sale revenue should land in 2027 rather than 2026; capex was up 100% YoY in the quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Management indicated that approximately 60% of this spending would be directed toward servers, with the remaining 40% allocated to data centers and networking equipment. ... The company expects most revenue from TPU (Tensor Processing Unit) system sales to materialize in 2027 rather than 2026 ... the company's capital expenditures surged to $44.9 billion in the quarter—a 100% increase from the prior year.

key_facts.fact: Sundar Pichai said Google offers 'the industry's broadest range of accelerators,' including Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform and Google's TPU 8t and 8i, plus a Virgo Network that can link a million accelerators across sites into one supercomputer.
key_facts.excerpt: We offer the industry's broadest range of accelerators from Google and NVIDIA, including the new NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, and TPU 8t and 8i, which deliver strong price performance. ... Our Virgo Network ... allows customers to connect a million AI accelerators across multiple data center sites into a unified supercomputer.

stories.headline: Georgia Power signs 25-year, 3.2-gigawatt deal to feed OpenAI's new Georgia data center

key_facts.fact: Southern Company subsidiary Georgia Power said on July 22 it signed a 25-year power supply agreement with OpenAI for a new project in Effingham County, Georgia.
key_facts.excerpt: July 22 : Southern Company's subsidiary said on Wednesday it has signed a 25-year power supply agreement with OpenAI for a new project in Effingham County, Georgia.

key_facts.fact: The facility is expected to need approximately 3,200 MW of power, and OpenAI agreed to provide up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response, cutting usage when the grid is stressed.
key_facts.excerpt: In addition, OpenAI, which is expected to need approximately 3,200 megawatts (MW) of power for its new facility, has agreed to provide up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response where it will reduce its power use in times of high demand, meaningfully supporting reliability across Georgia Power's system.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI will pay the full infrastructure and electric service costs to serve its facility and provide financial assurances designed to protect Georgia Power's other customers.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI will pay the full infrastructure and electric service costs to serve its facility and will fulfill requirements for long-term energy contracts and include financial assurances designed to protect Georgia Power customers.

key_facts.fact: Under the agreement Georgia Power can curtail energy delivered to the OpenAI site at certain times to support grid stability, letting the utility build fewer new generation resources.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the 25-year agreement, Georgia Power will have the ability to reduce energy delivered to the OpenAI facility during certain times to support the stability and reliability of the electric grid. This demand response resource will also allow the company to invest in fewer new generation resources to serve future growth.

key_facts.fact: The site, dubbed 'Project Camellia,' is about 45 minutes from Savannah; power is to be delivered in phases between 2028 and 2032, and the campus will use a closed-loop water cooling system.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is planning a major data center in Effingham County, Georgia, called "Project Camellia." The company signed a deal with Georgia Power for 3.2 gigawatts of electricity to be delivered in phases between 2028 and 2032. The company says it will cover all costs itself, so local power bills won't go up. The privately funded project will use a closed-loop water cooling system meant to keep ongoing water use low.

key_facts.fact: Georgia Power says the project should create thousands of construction and permanent on-site jobs and hundreds of millions of dollars in state and local tax revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: The project is expected to create thousands of construction and permanent on-site jobs, generate hundreds of millions of dollars in state and local tax revenue, and prioritize local contractors and businesses, Georgia Power said.

stories.headline: White House says China's Moonshot used banned Nvidia GB300 servers accessed in Thailand

key_facts.fact: White House OSTP director Michael Kratsios said on July 22 that Moonshot 'acquired GB300-equipped servers and has accessed GB300s in Thailand, likely to train its AI models,' arguing the company violated US export control rules.
key_facts.excerpt: The company "acquired GB300-equipped servers and has accessed GB300s in Thailand, likely to train its AI models," White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios said in a social media post Wednesday, making the case that Moonshot violated US export control rules and companies' terms of service to build its product.

key_facts.fact: The GB300 is among Nvidia's most advanced systems, built on Blackwell chips that cannot be sold to China; the highest-level chip currently receiving US licenses is the H200.
key_facts.excerpt: The GB300 is some of Nvidia's most advanced technology, containing its Blackwell chips, which are not allowed to be sold to China. The highest-level chip currently receiving licenses from the administration is the H200.

key_facts.fact: Kratsios also alleged Moonshot distilled Anthropic's Fable model to produce Kimi K3, the open model released last week that the company claims rivals top US systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Michael Kratsios, the director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, said the administration has information that Moonshot AI distilled Anthropic's Fable to produce Kimi K3. ... The release of Moonshot's Kimi model last week ... has raised concerns about whether China is closing in on America's lead in AI.

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned the day before that the administration could sanction China over intellectual property theft, saying US watermarks are turning up in Chinese models.
key_facts.excerpt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent separately warned Tuesday that the Trump administration could sanction China over intellectual property theft if they are found to be "stealing from our great companies." "We are finding ... marks of our U.S. large language models on many of the Chinese models, and that that's unacceptable"

key_facts.fact: Kratsios posted the accusation on X; the claim is that Moonshot reached restricted Blackwell hardware through Thailand-based infrastructure rather than direct imports.
key_facts.excerpt: Michael Kratsios, the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy director, writes on X that Moonshot accessed Nvidia's high-end GB300 processors in Thailand, which are subject to strict export controls.

key_facts.fact: Independent summaries of the post note the same wording, with Kratsios saying Moonshot 'acquired GB300-equipped servers and accessed GB300s in Thailand, likely to train its AI models.'
key_facts.excerpt: Yesterday, Director of the White House OSTP Michael Kratsios said: "Moonshot AI distilled Anthropic's Fable for the development of its K3 model." He added that the Chinese company acquired GB300-equipped servers and accessed GB300s in Thailand, likely to train its AI models.

stories.headline: IBM buys HRL Laboratories from Boeing and GM, adding silicon-spin qubits to its quantum stack

key_facts.fact: IBM announced on July 23 a definitive agreement to acquire HRL Laboratories, the Malibu research institution jointly owned by Boeing and General Motors; both will keep partnering with IBM on quantum work after the deal.
key_facts.excerpt: ARMONK, NY and MALIBU, CA, July 23, 2026 -- IBM today announced it has signed a definitive agreement to acquire HRL Laboratories, LLC (HRL), a flagship research and development institution. HRL is a private company jointly owned by Boeing and General Motors. Both Boeing and GM will continue to partner with IBM on quantum applications and advanced technology development following the transaction.

key_facts.fact: Financial terms were not disclosed; the transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and is expected to close by the end of Q3 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Financial details of the transaction were not disclosed, and IBM's acquisition of HRL is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals. The transaction is anticipated to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026.

key_facts.fact: The deal gives IBM a second qubit technology — electron spin qubits — alongside its superconducting approach, in what Reuters describes as a two-track quantum strategy.
key_facts.excerpt: IBM has agreed to buy HRL Laboratories, a private quantum computing research lab jointly owned by Boeing Co and General Motors, the company said on Thursday, adding a second pillar to IBM's quantum computing efforts. ... HRL, the former research arm of aerospace firm Hughes Aircraft based near Malibu, California, makes electron spin quantum circuits called 'qubits.'

key_facts.fact: IBM research director Jay Gambetta said HRL has 'a very strong spin qubit team, the strongest in the world,' and that HRL's chips, currently made in California, will start being produced at IBM's New York facility.
key_facts.excerpt: "They (HRL) have a very strong spin qubit team, the strongest in the world. ... I would not pursue a second path that was not built on a foundation that could be integrated together." ... HRL's team, which currently makes chips at its California facility, will start to make chips at IBM's cutting-edge facility in New York.

key_facts.fact: IBM said the acquisition can be paired with Anderon, the pure-play quantum wafer foundry it announced in May 2026 with US Department of Commerce support, potentially to manufacture spin qubits at scale.
key_facts.excerpt: In May 2026, IBM further expanded its quantum leadership when the ... would establish Anderon, the world's first pure-play quantum wafer foundry. ... Anderon is being created with the support of the U.S. Department of Commerce ... The acquisition of HRL offers an opportunity to partner even more closely with Anderon, including potential plans to develop spin qubit manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: Silicon quantum-dot spin qubits are CMOS-compatible and run at around 1 kelvin versus the millikelvin needed for superconducting qubits, with smaller circuits allowing higher chip density; IBM keeps its roadmap of Quantum Starling (about 200 logical qubits) in 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: The group works with silicon quantum-dot spin qubits that are compatible with standard CMOS manufacturing. Silicon spin qubits operate at a warmer temperature of around 1 kelvin, compared to the millikelvin required by superconducting qubits. The circuits are also much smaller, enabling higher chip density. ... Quantum Starling, the first large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer with about 200 logical qubits, is scheduled for release in 2029.

stories.headline: STMicro falls 14% on soft Q3 guidance even as it doubles down on AI data-center chips

key_facts.fact: STMicroelectronics reported second-quarter core profit below expectations and guided Q3 revenue slightly below consensus on July 23, sending shares down 14%.
key_facts.excerpt: July 23 (Reuters) - STMicroelectronics reported second-quarter core profit below market expectations and forecast third-quarter revenue slightly below analyst estimates on Thursday, sending its shares down 14%.

key_facts.fact: The company guided to Q3 revenue of $3.70 billion, plus or minus 3.5%, versus an average analyst estimate of $3.72 billion; even after the drop the stock is up more than 110% this year.
key_facts.excerpt: STMicro forecast third-quarter revenue of $3.70 billion, plus or minus 3.5%, versus analysts' average estimate of $3.72 billion, according to LSEG data. ... Including Thursday's fall, the stock is still up more than 110% this year.

key_facts.fact: Q2 net revenues were $3.49 billion with a 34.8% gross margin and $187 million of operating income; Q3 gross margin is guided to about 37.0%.
key_facts.excerpt: Q226 net revenues at $3.49 billion; Gross margin at 34.8% (non-U.S. GAAP gross margin at 35.2%); Operating income at $187 million ... Business outlook at mid-point: Q326 net revenues of $3.70 billion and gross margin of 37.0%.

key_facts.fact: STMicro raised its data-center revenue ambition to above $1 billion in 2026 and 'well above $2 billion' in 2027, citing continued strong AI data-center demand.
key_facts.excerpt: Driven by continued strong demand in AI datacenters, we are raising our revenue ambition for datacenters. Revenues are now expected above $1 billion in 2026 and, assuming the current dynamic continues and with the current engagements we have, well above $2 billion in 2027.

key_facts.fact: Management expects Q4 revenue above $4 billion, driven by customer programs in AI data centers and low-Earth-orbit satellite communications.
key_facts.excerpt: We anticipate a revenue growth acceleration in Q4, mainly driven by our engaged customer programs in AI datacenters and LEO satellite communication. We expect Q4 revenues to be above $4 billion, this translates into a H2 vs H1 growth above our normal 15% seasonality.

key_facts.fact: Group EBITDA of $679 million came in about 15% below the $797.7 million analysts expected, a bigger miss than the revenue shortfall; Jefferies tied the guidance miss partly to a slower iPhone 18 ramp.
key_facts.excerpt: Group EBITDA reached $679 million, falling short of the $797.7 million anticipated by analysts. The 15% shortfall exceeded the miss seen in third-quarter sales.
